_comment: Backfill for r20261113-2118 (bench 6: the adaptive form of the vote fix, arm file final-adaptive with quorum_exec_block_starved_rounds 4, on bench 5's disk, Hyperdisk Balanced at 20,000 provisioned IOPS; otherwise r20261113-1351's build and configuration), published with: bash benchmark/launch/launch.sh tasks/bench6/r20261113-2118/bench6-run3.env bundle --compare r20261113-1351 --backfill benchmark/report/backfill/2026-11-13-bench6-adaptive-20k.json. Sources: tasks/bench6-report-r20261113-1351.md sections 1 to 8 and benchmark/private/bench6-r20261113-2118/A7/comparison.md for every statement and figure (figure-by-figure notes in tasks/checkpoint-bench7-P1.md); the run's own manifest.json for recovery.node, recovery.killed_utc and recovery.restarted_utc (the chaos block's ts fields, the same ones kpis.recovery reads, so the merge is silent) and for fleet (machine type, zones, disk, blasters). recovery.rejoined_utc, recovery.catch_up_secs and recovery.failed_reports are null: make_bundle computes them from the tn_node_mode series and the batch-seal failure counter, which the sources above do not give; the node log's kill-to-active times are in the caveats instead. Written 2026-11-14.
title: The adaptive vote fix on Hyperdisk Balanced at 20,000 IOPS
summary: We repeated r20261113-1351 with one change: the vote fix ran in its adaptive form instead of the always-on form. In the adaptive form a header names the author's own executed tip until one of the author's headers is cancelled uncertified; the author then uses the always-on quorum rule, never more than 8 outputs behind its tip, inside a starved window of up to 128 rounds, and afterwards tries its own tip again. The build (2df831e3c), the other three switches, bench 5's fleet and disk (Hyperdisk Balanced at 20,000 provisioned IOPS), the load and the chaos plan were the same. Throughput and what binds did not change: average chain throughput with all ten generators running was 5,394.6 tx/s against 5,322.1 (+1.4 %, inside the always-on run's own five-minute range), the disks again sat at their limit of 20,000 writes a second (0.999) with every engine busy, and the median time to seen was 12.89 s against 12.99 s. The epoch closes and the killed validator's rejoin matched too. Own-header certification was a little lower: 99.64 % over the load blast against 99.94 %, and before the kill validators 02, 06 and 10 (London, the Netherlands and Mumbai) sat at 98.8 to 98.9 %, about 1 point under and outside the always-on run's range for them. The loss is the adaptive form's probe: those three spent 95.7 to 97.4 % of their headers in starved windows, and every return to the own tip lost a header. In exchange, headers named a block about 0.9 s old on average, against 5.5 s. The senders paid more: 104,280 transactions were resent after the generators' 300-s gap check against 29,546, and 10,767 never landed against 183, through the same reordering of re-queued batches as under the always-on form (issue #1807), exposed on more validators in more minutes. No node logged a halt, fork, unexpected execution result, fatal database error or panic. This run is one of four in one program, one node build with two forms of the vote fix on two disks: the always-on form as r20261113-1351 (20,000 IOPS) and r20261113-1630 (50,000 IOPS), the adaptive form as r20261113-2118 (20,000 IOPS) and r20261114-0000 (50,000 IOPS). Across them the form changed neither throughput nor what binds; the always-on form certified slightly more own headers at 20,000 IOPS, neither form held certification at 50,000 IOPS (the adaptive run certified more), the adaptive form's senders paid more on both disks through the same reordering (issue #1807), and which form goes upstream is not decided.

evidence_detail: Commit 2df831e3c is the head of the branch bench/bench6-2026-11, built for this benchmark: a base commit 165e3fe01 plus 98 commits, in which every fix for bench 5's concerns is a node switch, off by default. The twelve switches are quorum_exec_block (the vote fix, whose form the setting quorum_exec_block_starved_rounds picks), vote_queue_fix, epoch_record_state_check, mdbx_random_advice, mdbx_no_writemap, sealed_tx_keep, digest_dedupe, recovery_threads, epoch_close_task_drain, pipelined_persist, rpc_admission_backlog_outputs and parent_grace. A node logs its switches at every start ('node switches') and exports them as tn_node_switch. The image was named by registry digest (adiri@sha256:874537ff…852745) and ran all four runs of this program unchanged.

fleet.label: c3-highcpu-8 + Hyperdisk Balanced at 20,000 IOPS (c3-hdb), ten regions, validator-05 in Ashburn

load.placement: one blaster per validator, in that validator's zone, sending only to it

methodology: All four runs of this program used one node image, built from the branch bench/bench6-2026-11 at commit 2df831e3c (a base commit 165e3fe01 plus 98 commits), with sub-second timestamps from genesis, and named by registry digest (adiri@sha256:874537ff…852745). Nothing was rebuilt between the runs. Every fix in that build is a node switch, off by default; a node logs its switches at every start ('node switches') and exports them as the metric tn_node_switch. The load generator was built from tn-transaction-generator commit 62bbd5f.

The vote fix is the switch quorum_exec_block. Instead of its own newest executed block, a proposer names in each header a block that a quorum of validators should already have executed; a voter signs only after it finds the named block in its own chain. The setting quorum_exec_block_starved_rounds picks the form. With 0, the always-on form, every header takes the quorum value over the author's own executed tip and the blocks its parent headers named, capped at the own tip and never more than 8 outputs behind it (the floor); in practice nearly every header named the author's tip minus 8 outputs. With 4, the adaptive form, a header names the author's own tip until one of the author's headers is cancelled uncertified; the author then uses the always-on rule inside a starved window of up to 128 rounds, and afterwards tries its own tip again.

Three more switches were on in all four runs: vote_queue_fix (the voter's lock wait), epoch_record_state_check (a check of the closing state when an epoch record is built) and mdbx_random_advice (the MDBX database's random-access hint over the whole file). The other eight stayed at their defaults: mdbx_no_writemap, sealed_tx_keep, digest_dedupe, recovery_threads, epoch_close_task_drain, pipelined_persist, rpc_admission_backlog_outputs and parent_grace. The switch set came from an arm file applied at deployment, before the nodes' coordinated start: no arm walk, no cache eviction and no restart before the load. Each node first ran once, alone, during staging (17 to 90 s, every switch at its default, no peer reached, no output executed); the switches of the run were on from the coordinated start, the first process that executed blocks.

Each run created ten validators and one observer on c3-highcpu-8 (8 vCPU, 16 GiB), each node with one 100 GB Hyperdisk Balanced disk for the root and the data directory at 800 MiB/s, provisioned at 20,000 IOPS (bench 5's disk) or 50,000 IOPS. One validator ran in each of bench 5's ten regions (Los Angeles, London, Sydney, Tokyo, Ashburn, the Netherlands, Singapore, Hong Kong, Seoul and Mumbai), the observer in Los Angeles. Epochs last 1,200 s.

Each run had three blasts. Ten generators on e2-standard-2, one per validator in that validator's zone and sending only to it, ran blast 0, the floor, with 8 senders each and up to 16 transactions in flight per sender (8 x 16); blast 1 with 600 senders and a window of 4 (600 x 4, at most 24,000 in flight); and blast 2, the load blast, with 600 senders and a window of 16 (600 x 16, at most 96,000 in flight) and phases of 120 s warm-up, 2,400 s mixed load and 180 s cool-down, the shape of bench 5's load blast.

The chaos plan was bench 5's, inside blast 2: validator-05's container was killed with SIGKILL shortly before an epoch boundary and held down for 300 s, so the outage crossed the boundary; then it was started, and the observer was restarted 300 s after that. Generator 05 sends only to validator-05 and does not fail over to another endpoint, so it is cut off for the outage and for as long as its validator follows the chain afterwards.

Headline figures keep bench 5's definitions and code; bench 5's throughput, latency and landing figures quoted on these pages were recomputed exactly from bench 5's own generator documents with the same code, while its certification, disk, stage and rejoin figures come from bench 5's report or from this program's reading of bench 5's logs and model. Throughput is the chain's transactions per second over the window in which all ten generators ran, with the outage and generator 05 inside it. Time to seen runs from submission until the generator saw the receipt, from the generators' summed histograms (the bundle method); time to land is to the block's timestamp, in whole seconds, so about 0.5 s low. Own-header certification is the share of a validator's own headers that were certified, over blast 2's mixed phase unless another window is named.

The analysis read every node's whole main log (the node's stderr file was not pulled) and the node metrics exported from Prometheus before each teardown. The comparison of the two forms ran the same scripts on both runs of a disk and reproduced the always-on runs' figures.

Against r20261113-1351 only the form of the vote fix changed: the arm file final-adaptive set quorum_exec_block_starved_rounds to 4 instead of 0, with the same other switches. The image, the generator, the fleet, the disk, the load and the chaos plan are the same.

A first deployment, r20261113-2044, stopped before the coordinated start and before the arm was applied: validator-08's first start, during staging, failed with 'Address already in use' on its worker listener. It was torn down and is not part of the run.

Times are UTC on 13 November. Deployment ran from 21:18:25 to 22:02:14 (the second deployment); all eleven nodes started at one due time, with 0 s spread. The fsync probe median was 1,043 µs, with validators 04 and 07 flagged slow. The mixed phases ran 22:12:55-22:19:56 (blast 0), 22:25:37-22:33:06 (blast 1) and 22:45:46-23:25:56 (blast 2). Validator-05 was killed at 23:08:59 and started at 23:13:59, epoch 5 opened during its outage at 23:09:58, and the observer was restarted at 23:18:59.

The teardown ended with rc 0 at 23:52:55, 12 instances deleted and none left. The archive holds 625 files, 2.48 GB. The metric export before the teardown holds 382 metrics (21,023 series) but lacks validator-07's vote-stage series, so the voter's lock wait here comes from the log, and no comparison figure rests on that series alone. Before the kill the mixed phase ran 1,393 s here against 1,477 s in r20261113-1351; where windows differ, only rates and shares are compared.
caveats: Against r20261113-1351 (ranges are that run's own variation): blast 2 throughput 5,394.6 against 5,322.1 tx/s (+1.4 %; its five-minute blocks 4,718.8 to 5,616.9) and 5,030.1 against 5,066.9 tx/s without generator 05; blast 1 (600 x 4) 6,242.5 against 6,380.8 tx/s (-2.2 %; its 60-s blocks 6,025.2 to 6,638.3); time to seen p50/p95 12.89/28.76 s against 12.99/30.89 s; time to land p95/p99 6.79/28.39 s against 14.66/61.91 s; executed rate per node 5,399 against 5,314 tx/s; engine task 184.5 against 187.2 µs per transaction; device writes 0.999 against 0.998 of 20,000 a second, 3.71 against 3.74 per transaction; transactions per output 4,072 against 3,854 (+5.7 %). With one run per form, a difference inside the always-on run's range is not told apart from noise. Why the land tail was shorter here was not measured.

The one throughput exception is the floor blast: 684.7 tx/s against 700.3, 9.5 tx/s under the always-on run's lowest block. Generators 02 and 06 landed 3 % of the other eight's median against 11 % and 12 %, with no resends and no skipped transactions in either run. In blasts 0 and 1 the generators' start spread was 59 to 89 s against 23 to 48 s in r20261113-1351, as generators 02 and 06 began their mixed phase late after losing setup transactions in the preamble; the cause was not traced. The floor's seen p50 was 1.63 s against 1.65 s.

At 20,000 IOPS both forms ran the device at its write limit with the engines busy 994 to 996 ms a second; one analysis calls this disk-bound and another engine-bound with the device at its limit, and the measurements agree. In minutes 30 to 39 this run executed 5,103 tx/s against 4,839 (+5.5 %), with outputs 14.9 % larger: at the pinned device, larger outputs cost fewer writes per transaction.

Over blast 2's mixed phase the fleet certified 99.64 % of own headers against 99.94 %; the lowest validator was validator-02 at 99.0 % against validator-06 at 99.7 %. Before the kill validators 02, 06 and 10 certified 98.9, 98.9 and 98.8 % against 100, 99.8 and 99.9 %, outside the always-on run's five-minute range for each. In blast 2's first 120 s the fleet certified 97.98 % against 100.0 %, with six validators under 99 % (lowest validator-02, 96.3 %). Votes refused as execution-behind: 15 against 0. Vote timeouts: none in either run, and the voter's lock wait was 0 at the 95th percentile in both.

Before the kill the adaptive form named the author's own tip on 66.1 % of headers (always-on 0.2 %), on average 1.21 outputs behind the tip (about 0.9 s) against 7.59 (about 5.5 s). Validators 02, 06 and 10 had 95.7 to 97.4 % of their own headers inside a starved window and entered one 78 to 83 times an hour; inside they certified 99.81 to 99.95 %, outside 56.6 to 77.9 %, and every return to the own tip lost a header (1.19 to 1.39 per return). That a one-output lead fails the tip header within a 353-ms round is inferred. The slow voters (05, 04 and 03) answered 'superseded' 3,164 times before the kill against 85, on others' own-tip headers; 2,747 of the 3,148 answers joined to a header fell on headers that certified anyway. Rounds were 1.1 % slower before the kill: the certify stage took 14 ms longer, as the window's quorum headers certified later (p50 0.287 against 0.171 s), and the proposer's minimum delay absorbed most of it. The lead over the seventh validator never reached the floor at this disk (0.01 to 0.02 % of headers), so the floor had nothing to absorb, and the always-on rule on this run's tips predicts 99.8 to 100 % per validator (arithmetic). What the fresher named block is worth downstream was not measured.

In blast 2's first 120 s the adaptive form certified less on both disks. No analysis joined that window per header. The window state resets at each epoch and after 64 certified tip headers, which fits every author naming its own tip when the load begins; that was not tested.

Blast 2: gap resends 104,280 against 29,546, from eight generators against three (02, 06 and 10); 'nonce too high' skips 52,588 against 13,036; validator-minutes with an exposed lost own header 104 against 23; transactions unlanded after the 180-s tail scan 10,767 against 183 (9,290 against 0 with generator 05 left out); landings seen 300 s or more after submission 111,508 against 40,263; landed over accepted 99.9267 % against 99.9987 %. The adaptive form had 3.54 times the resends (generator 05 left out), 4.03 times the skips and 59 times the unlanded (all generators). Blast 1 (600 x 4) also had 2,016 gap resends and 5,875 unlanded transactions against 0 and 1,665. The mechanism is the same in all four runs of this program and is tracked as issue #1807: when an own header is cancelled or committed late, its batches are queued again behind batches a newer own header already carried, so the sender's later transactions are skipped at execution as 'nonce too high', sit in no pool, and land only after the generator resends its window at its 300-s gap check. The pool switches sealed_tx_keep and digest_dedupe were off in all four runs; whether they change this cost was not measured in these runs (in the earlier arm-walk run, sealed_tx_keep with three other switches on left no gap resends, a reading confounded with the other switches and an epoch boundary). Every gap-resend second of generators 01-04 and 06-10 fell 280 to 345 s after a lost own header of the generator's own validator (124 of 124 seconds here, 31 of 31 in r20261113-1351). The first resend wave opened from the near validators' cancelled own-tip headers in blast 2's warm-up (22:43:59-22:45:10). The adaptive form exposed the loss on more validators in more minutes; that this breadth sets the totals is an inference. The whole difference in the senders' cost between the forms sits in that reordering loss, a mechanism both forms share.

Validator-05 rejoined by the same rule: 22 min 39.8 s from the kill to active against 21 min 40.7 s, a difference the schedule explains (the load ran 58 s longer after the kill), and 5 min 02.8 s from the cool-down's end to promotion against 5 min 01.9 s. All six epoch closes certified on one record hash and one closing block on all eleven nodes; the fewest signers per epoch were 10, 10, 9, 7, 8 and 9 (always-on 10, 10, 7, 7, 9 and 9), the first quorum at the two blast-2 closes came at 14.85 and 13.85 s (16.44 and 14.75 s), and the loaded closes' highest execution lag was 20, 38 and 42 rounds (38, 52 and 48). No node logged a halt, fork, unexpected execution result, fatal database text or panic.

The restarted observer took 6 min 00.4 s to its first line at distance 1 and 7 min 12 s to follow output by output, against 23.3 s in r20261113-1351. The adaptive run at 50,000 IOPS (r20261114-0000) took 5.1 s, so the data does not tie this to the form; the cause is unknown, nothing was lost, and closing blocks and record hashes matched.

The earlier arm-walk run of the same build (r20261112-1520) had read the always-on form at 84.6 % in its warm-up against the adaptive form's 96.3 %, at different cache states. That order did not recur here, where the adaptive form was lower in blast 2's first 120 s on both disks; the windows differ.
The teardown's provenance check warns 'node startup provenance mismatch' in all four runs: each node's start during staging ran before the arm file was applied. It is known and not a finding.

At 20,000 IOPS the always-on form is ahead on both own-header certification and the senders' cost. The adaptive form's gain is the fresher named block, whose value downstream was not measured; it paid for it with about 1.1 % of headers lost to the probe on each windowed author and 3.5 times the resends.

Not measured: run-to-run variance at this disk, when a vote reaches its author (not logged), what the age of the named block costs, the senders' cost with sealed_tx_keep or digest_dedupe on, why the land tail was shorter here, and the cause of the late generator starts. The probe's parameters (the 128-round bound and the 64-header streak) were not varied.

Each configuration ran once (one run per form and disk), so run-to-run variation is not measured. The form of the vote fix is not decided: at 20,000 IOPS the always-on form certified a little more and cost the senders less, at 50,000 IOPS neither form held certification, and the floor's depth has been tested only as arithmetic. A further run of both forms is planned on a build of the newer upstream main branch, which uses a different execution storage engine (tn-lmdb) than these runs (MDBX), with a candidate fix for issue #1807 added; its result is not known.
